title: Brioche
subtitle: a rich, buttery French bread with a fine, tender crumb
excerpt: Brioche is bread enriched with eggs and butter until it sits closer to cake than loaf. The dough is soft and sticky -- it needs long kneading and a cold overnight rest to develop the right structure. It is worth every step.
sourceNotes: Classic French enriched bread. Brioche a tete is the traditional shaped version; this is a tin loaf.

recipe.freezeNotes: Slice and freeze. Defrost at room temperature or toast from frozen.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The dough must be made ahead -- it requires an overnight rest in the fridge before shaping.

content.text: The butter goes in last, added a little at a time once the dough is smooth. Do not rush this stage. The dough will look greasy and odd at first. Keep going and it will come together into something glossy and elastic.
Mix the yeast with the warm milk and a pinch of sugar. Leave 5 minutes. Combine flour, sugar, and salt in a large bowl.
Add the yeast mixture and beaten eggs to the flour. Mix to a rough dough. Turn out and knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Add the butter a few cubes at a time, kneading each addition in fully before adding more. This will take 10 to 15 minutes. The finished dough will be soft, glossy, and slightly sticky.
Place in an oiled bowl, cover, and leave at room temperature for 1 hour until puffed. Transfer to the fridge overnight (or for at least 8 hours).
Remove from fridge. Shape into a log and place in a greased 900g loaf tin. Cover and prove at room temperature for 2 to 3 hours until the dough has risen above the rim.
Heat the oven to 180C. Brush the top with beaten egg. Bake for 28 to 30 minutes until deep golden. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out.

items.symptom: Dough will not absorb the butter
items.cause: Butter was too cold or added too quickly.
items.fix: The butter must be very soft -- like thick cream. Add it one piece at a time and wait until each piece disappears before adding the next.

items.symptom: Loaf is dense with a tight crumb
items.cause: Not proved for long enough at room temperature after shaping.
items.fix: Be patient with the final prove. The dough is cold from the fridge and needs a full 2 to 3 hours to relax and rise.

content.text: Brioche is a French enriched bread with roots in Normandy, where dairy and eggs were abundant. It sits at the crossroads of bread and patisserie. In France it is eaten at breakfast, used for pain perdu, and served alongside savoury dishes like foie gras. In Britain it appears on restaurant menus as burger buns and French toast.
